contract.known_boundary: Manage large local model artifacts through durable identity/version metadata, staged or resumable transfer, integrity verification, atomic promotion into readable storage, migration/rollback policy and explicit cleanup/quota handling.
contract.integrity_policy: A model must not become runtime-ready merely because a transfer completed. Expected digest and/or application-owned signature/format validation must succeed before atomic promotion; incomplete or rejected staging remains non-authoritative.
contract.secret_policy: Hub credentials and signed URLs are inputs to retrieval, not model-storage metadata. Tokens must be supplied through an approved secret provider and never copied into manifests, logs or durable transfer state.
contract.migration_policy: Migration must preserve the previously valid model until replacement bytes and metadata are verified. Version switches, partition moves and cleanup are distinct from download completion.
contract.raspberry_pi_policy: Linux compatibility can count for discovery only. Raspberry-Pi-specific filesystem, free-space, durability and performance validation remains mandatory before certification.

candidates.platform_basis: Upstream explicitly reports Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS tested. Raspberry Pi is counted only as Linux architecture-level discovery evidence.
functional_evidence: Hugging Face model/file and snapshot download APIs
cache layout separates refs, commit snapshots and content blobs
LFS cache blobs are identified by SHA-256
candidates.maturity_constraint: Upstream labels the Dart client work-in-progress and Flutter-dependent; Raspberry Pi is not tested explicitly.

candidates.platform_basis: Pure Dart storage supports Android via cellar_flutter, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux and CLI/server use; Raspberry Pi is architecture-level Linux/Dart evidence only.
functional_evidence: streaming write/read for large model weights with bounded memory
filesystem writes use temp-file then rename atomic promotion
partition copy/move and whole-partition migration APIs
persistent/cache/scratch lifecycle partitions and quota/age cleanup
materialization to a native file path for FFI model runtimes
candidates.known_constraint: Cellar is a local storage substrate, not a remote model downloader. Same-key concurrent writers must be serialized by the application. Cryptography is provided through an application-owned seam rather than bundled primitives.

candidates.platform_basis: Flutter-first foreground transfer component using portable Dart/Flutter dependencies. It is retained as native transfer/integrity research, not Raspberry Pi evidence.
functional_evidence: multipart HTTP range download with durable checkpoints and resume
single staged output with fallback when range requests are unavailable
custom application validator for signature/format policy
checksum or validation rejection discards staged state rather than exposing unverified output
restoration metadata intentionally excludes headers, cookies, bearer tokens and signed URLs
candidates.known_constraint: Foreground-oriented: it does not promise continued mobile transfer after OS termination. Background mobile adapters are out of scope/upstream future work.

research_findings.model_identity: huggingface_hub_dart provides a concrete revision-aware cache model using refs, commit snapshots and content blobs rather than one mutable filename.
research_findings.atomic_storage: cellar streams large objects without loading them fully into memory and performs native filesystem writes through a temporary file followed by rename, preserving the previous object after interrupted writes.
research_findings.migration: cellar exposes cross-partition moves and whole-partition migration, but an AI-Orchestrator model schema/version migration state machine remains application-owned and unvalidated.
research_findings.transfer_integrity: resumable_downloader provides durable HTTP-range checkpoints, SHA-256 and application validators before finalization; rejected staged state is discarded.
research_findings.security: cellar is fully CLEAR including SBOM/OSV. huggingface_hub_dart is REVIEW because it intentionally reads HF_TOKEN/HF_TOKEN_PATH. resumable_downloader has CLEAR source/supply-chain but REVIEW vulnerability status because primary dependency versions are not lock-resolved.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: Two Linux-level discovery families exist (cellar plus huggingface_hub_dart), but neither constitutes Raspberry-Pi board/filesystem/performance validation.

decision.next_action: Keep discovery depth closed while defining the provider-neutral model manifest/state machine: immutable model identity and revision, staging/checkpoints, expected digest/signature policy, atomic promotion, rollback/migration, quota cleanup and secret indirection. Then complete admission and target-specific runtime/filesystem tests.
